criterion: lease wall time at the bound <= 2x the build lease on the same repository
host: Docker Desktop linux/arm64, 1 CPU-bound python process, atlas-aci-dev-s16 image, python 3.12
method: synthetic fixture over a real graph (the dogfood run of the atlas-aci suite was cut: cut order step 6); synthetic coverage.py format-3 reports with real per-test context spelling over the python files of a 150-file copy of atlas-aci (mcp-server/src, mcp-server/tests; the 'storage' package is a default skip pattern and is not indexed), a sidecar made by the real coverage-manifest code, imported by the real importer; each size measured in a fresh interpreter, 5 reader-lease acquisitions (median), peak RSS from getrusage and tracemalloc peak of one acquisition
notes: the 200,000 point was cut: a generation above the shipped bound is also refused at lease time (block validation), so the bound cannot be silently exceeded by an operator-raised import limit
a 100k run in one report is rejected at the per-run bound (observed: run_limit), which is why the 100k point uses two runs
tiny repositories pay a larger ratio but a small absolute cost; the criterion is evaluated on a real 150-file repository

points.note: first measurement run; the per-run bound
noisy (host contention, 8.06-12.18 s samples); not used for the decision
the proposed per-generation bound (2 runs of 50,000)

result: at 99,960 test_executes (2 runs) the lease takes 8.60 s = 1.76x the 4.89 s build lease; peak RSS 396 MB vs 152 MB (+243 MB, about 2.4 KB per observation)
